---
title: "Labour Market Status Prediction"
format: html
---

```{r}
# Initial setup, dependency loading, and data preparation, as well as splitting the data into a training and validation set so that I don't have to use up submissions

library(httpgd)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(glmnet)
library(randomForest)
library(xgboost)
library(pROC)
library(ROCR)

# Setting the seed so that we have reproducible results
set.seed(2026)

# Visualization of the data
train_data <- read.csv("data/train.csv")
test_data <- read.csv("data/test.csv")

head(train_data)
head(test_data)

# Split training data into training and validation sets (60/40 split)

train_index <- createDataPartition(train_data$employed_status, 
                                   p = 0.6, 
                                   list = FALSE)

training_set <- train_data[train_index, ]
validation_set <- train_data[-train_index, ]

# Save validation set for later testing
write.csv(validation_set, "data/validation_set.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("Training set size:", nrow(training_set), "\n")
cat("Validation set size:", nrow(validation_set), "\n")
cat("Employment rate in training:", mean(training_set$employed_status), "\n")
cat("Employment rate in validation:", mean(validation_set$employed_status), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Quick EDA to understand your data
summary(training_set)

# Check for missing values
colSums(is.na(training_set))

# Employment status distribution
ggplot(training_set, aes(x = factor(employed_status))) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Employment Status Distribution",
       x = "Employed (1) vs Unemployed (0)",
       y = "Count")

# Visualize key variables (adjust column names as needed)
# Example: age distribution by employment status
if("age" %in% colnames(training_set)) {
  ggplot(training_set, aes(x = age, fill = factor(employed_status))) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
    labs(title = "Age Distribution by Employment Status")
}

# Correlation with employment status (for numeric variables)
numeric_cols <- training_set %>%
  select(where(is.numeric), employed_status) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs")

# See which numeric variables correlate most with employment
sort(abs(numeric_cols["employed_status", ]), decreasing = TRUE)
```
